text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

At least six Australian Rugby players are at risk of losing their position in the Test side for the November 9 clash, Wallaby coach Greg Smith revealed this week. Smith said the two prop spots were still up for grabs, as well as the second row position. The players have been warned they need to work hard to keep their positions on the side. Page 21.

Australian rugby players will wear black arm bands in their match tonight as a mark of respect to former Australian under-19 centre Ian Tucker who died from injuries sustained in a match in England over the weekend. The Wallabies will stand fora minute's silence before their first tour game in Scotland. Page 21.

The youngsters of the tennis circuit look set to dominate in January's Sydney International tennis tournament. While defending champions Monica Seles and Todd Martin will return to defend their titles, young players including Martina Hingis, Mark Philippoussis and Marcelo Rios will prove formidable opponents. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following the announcement Netball Australia will field an Australian Institute of Sport team in the 1998 national competition, funding cuts of almost A$500,000 were averted from an important netball development program. Two weeks ago, Netball Australia rfused to side a team in the competition and the Australian Sports Commission said the development programme would then be scrapped. Federal Sports Minister Warwick Smith said the AIS is now hopeful it could maintain its netball program as part of A$1 million in government funding. Page 48.

As relations between Soccer Australia and the Oceania Football Confederation reached their lowest point, Soccer Australia chairman David Hill was suspended from the Confederation's executive. The move followed Hill's criticism of the OFC and personal attaks on OFC president Charlie Dempsey. Page 48.

The Australian Golf Union has stepped up its preparation for the A$1 million Australian Open following massive public interest in Tiger Woods' first appearance outside America. The Open, which will be held in Sydney between November 21 and 24, has attractd a 40 percent increase in ticket sales and an increase in sales of corporate hospitality facilities. Page 47.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League's Carlton club will record another A$500,000-plus profit this year. The club recorded a A$581,000 profit in 1995 and their financial status has continued to grow, but the club is expecting a difficult year in 1997 as the salary cap increases by A$350,000. Page C15.

Australia's Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich is expected to be sidelined for a month after undergoing knee surgery on ligament damage resulting from last Saturday's match against Sunderland. Bosnich missed the first two months of the season from the same injury. Page C15.

Australian basketballer Andrew Gaze won his third successive National Basketball League most valuable player award last night, his fifth in six years. Gaze polled 135 to pip Canberra import Robert Rose on 128. North Melbourne's Daryl McDonald was third wih 114 votes. Page C16.
HERALD SUN

The career of the Australian Football League's Gary Ablett will be decided at his appearance at compulsory training at Kardinia Park tonight. It has been confirmed Ablett will be fined for breaching his contract by failing to appear at Geelong's opening pe-season training session on Monday. Page 88.

Queensland Bulls cricket coach John Buchanan has attacked allegations that Geoff Foley was guilty of chucking, claiming he is innocent. Foley and New South Wales medium pacer Brad McNamara were reported for the incident by umpires after a Mercantile Mutual game at the Gabba 12 days ago. The final decisions on the incident will be left to the players' respective state associations. Page 86.

As Australian Rugby League clubs met yesterday to discuss expanding the competition, it was revealed Melbourne and New Zealand were likely to be admitted into the fold in 1998. In the wake of the Super League court appeal victory, the ARL met with chairmen of the remaining 12 clubs in the competition to map out the future of the game. Page 85.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Melbourne Cup favourite Oscar Schindler has attracted controversy this week, with other trainers complaining about the horse's weight. Gai Waterhouse was one of a number of leading trainers who complained about the favourite's under weight-for-age, and practically conceded victory to the horse. Page 80.

Australian horse trainer Bart Cummings has announced his Cox Plate winner Saintly will contest both the Melbourne Cup and the Japan Cup. Saintly has never won in a race distancing over 2040m, but Cummings is confident the four-year-old will prove strong in the Melbourne Cup next week. Page 76.

Australian basketballer Andrew Gaze graduated with a science degree yesterday from Victoria University. After juggling basketball with study, Gaze finally received his degree 11 years after enrolling and only three days away from the NBL championship. Page 75.
